title: How to make a Wi-Fi QR code guests can scan
excerpt: A Wi-Fi QR code lets people join your network without typing the password. How to make one, what the fields mean, and how to get it to scan first time.

title: What actually makes a password strong
excerpt: Strength is not about odd symbols; it is about length and randomness. What matters, and how to get it without inventing anything yourself.

title: How to fix messy JSON and read the error
excerpt: When JSON will not parse, the error can be blunt. How to make a file readable, find the character that is breaking it, and minify it once it is valid.

title: How to read a cron expression without guessing
excerpt: Cron's five fields are easy to misread. What each one means, the symbols that trip people up, and how to check a schedule before you rely on it.

title: How to compress an image without it going blurry
excerpt: Compression trades file size against detail. How to shrink a JPG or WebP while keeping it looking right, and which format to reach for.

title: What Base64 is for, and what it is not
excerpt: Base64 turns binary data into plain text so it can travel through channels built for text. What it does, what it does not, and when to reach for it.

title: Knowing how long your text is, as you write it
excerpt: Word and character limits are everywhere, and eyeballing them does not work. A quick way to keep both counts in view while you draft.

title: Where your files go when you use an online tool
excerpt: Most online tools upload your file to a server to process it. NoByte does the work in your browser instead. What that difference means, and how to check it.
